The circuit on the right side is a voltage source Vs connected through a resistor R and an ideal diode to a capacitor C, and the capacitor voltage is labeled Vc. Reasoning: From the given R = 500 Ω, C = 10 μF, so the time constant RC = 500 × 10 μF = 500 × 10×10^-6 s = 5 ms. The period T = 4 ms, therefore T/2 = 2 ms. According to the waveform in the figure, from 0 to 2 ms, Vs = +10 V, the capacitor is initially uncharged, the ideal diode conducts, and the capacitor charges according to Vc(t) = 10(1 - exp(-t/RC)). Therefore Vc(2 ms) = 10(1 - exp(-2/5)) = 10(1 - exp(-0.4)) ≈ 10(1 - 0.6703) = 3.2968 V. From 2 ms to 3 ms, the source voltage becomes -10 V, the diode is reverse biased, and the capacitor has no discharge path, so Vc remains at the value at 2 ms. Therefore Vc(3 ms) ≈ 3.2968 V, rounded to one decimal place as 3.3 V.
